name: How much equity is needed for ground-up multifamily development in Los Angeles?

mainEntity.name: How much cash equity do developers usually need to start a new multifamily project in Los Angeles?
mainEntity.text: How much cash equity do developers usually need to start a new multifamily project in Los Angeles?

acceptedAnswer.text: Equity requirements for ground-up multifamily development in Los Angeles usually fall in the 25% to 40% range of total project cost, but that range can move depending on the site and sponsor. Unentitled land, difficult zoning, expensive parking solutions, and higher construction types often push equity needs higher. Lenders also look at borrower track record, guaranteed completion strength, loan-to-cost, and whether the project has a viable exit strategy after stabilization. If the deal is especially risky, lenders may ask for additional contingency reserves, interest reserves, or subordinate capital. For a developer, the key question is not only how much equity is needed, but when it must be injected. Some projects require land acquisition cash up front, then staged equity deposits during design, permitting, and construction. A realistic capital stack should include acquisition, soft costs, hard costs, contingency, financing fees, and lease-up reserves.
acceptedAnswer.description: Many Los Angeles construction lenders expect roughly 25% to 40% of total project cost as equity, though the exact amount depends on land basis, borrower experience, preleasing, and project risk. More complex or unentitled sites usually require more cash. Higher leverage is less common on small urban infill projects.
